title: Tide of Mafeking enthusiasm
html_source: The Siege of Mafeking (1899-1900) took place in the eponymous South African town during the Second Boer War and led to an upsurge of patriotism when the Prime Minister Lord Robert Cecil’s son (among others trapped by the Siege) was freed by the efforts of Robert Baden-Powell (of Boy Scouts fame). Despite the morale boost for England, the Seige (and Relief) had little military significance, but the reference would have been clear at the time of writing (and the time during which the novel is set).
